scope: Read-only review of the isolated frozen-Stem ten-update QAT control wrapper, its unit test, inherited base-runner paths, prospective cache/source/protocol closure, checkpoint/export invariants, watchdog launch, and generic development17 evaluator compatibility. The reviewer did not start the CPU integration gate, initialize CUDA, use a GPU, train, evaluate, or modify production source.

verdict.summary: No unresolved blocker was found for the single fresh execute() path. The wrapper changes only the optimizer/clipping parameter set by freezing stem.conv weight and bias; inherited state_dict/named_parameters, replay, cache, SGD hyperparameters, source FP32 checkpoint, maxabs package, watchdog, checkpoint/resume, and export paths remain intact. The one review finding about weak semantic binding of preparatory JSON artifacts was fixed before the coordinator started the CPU gate.

review_findings.finding: The first reviewed version accepted the prior decision using only update count/continue_training and accepted the gradient inspection using only optimizer_updates/finite_gradients. A stale or substituted JSON artifact could therefore be hashed into the new identity without proving it belonged to the intended rejected QAT run and unchanged base inputs.
review_findings.current_resolution: prepare() now requires the exact prior experiment id, rejected development17 status, selected FP32 checkpoint hash, complete inspection identity, complete base protocol, and exact source closure including the inspection script. The final wrapper identity additionally binds hashes of both JSON artifacts.
review_findings.execution_decision: The coordinator-owned CPU gate was started only after this fix, so its identity is based on the corrected source.

positive_checks: FrozenStemQAT.parameters() filters only tensors whose requires_grad is false; make_model() marks only stem.conv weight and bias false. The inherited named_parameters() and state_dict() keep all 134 parameters while parameters() yields the 132 trainable parameters (train_qat_frozen_stem.py:25-39).

The inherited update path obtains gradients, divides by the update-wide foreground count, clips, steps, and clears gradients only through model.parameters(); therefore the frozen Stem is excluded from gradient validation, clipping, SGD, weight decay, and momentum state while the other 132 parameters follow the unchanged base algorithm (train_qat.py:105-148).

The wrapper update snapshots both Stem tensors before every update, checks exact equality afterward, requires no gradient and no optimizer state for either tensor, and records per-update evidence (train_qat_frozen_stem.py:73-83).

Checkpointing still uses the inherited full state_dict(), so both frozen tensors remain in update_0000 through update_0010 and in any resume checkpoint. Completion validates all ten candidate states against the frozen replay cursor and compares each Stem tensor bit-exactly with update_0000 (train_qat.py:151-157; train_qat_frozen_stem.py:121-131).

Completion also requires every history row to contain frozen_stem_unchanged, binds last.pt to the worker event, requires export parity, and compares every exported INT8/INT32 field of stem.conv with the original maxabs package (train_qat_frozen_stem.py:121-142).

install() redirects the inherited base OUT, RUN, CPU gate, prepare, model factory, and update callback in the worker process. execute() launches the wrapper module itself, so the subprocess receives the same process-local adapter instead of silently running the unfrozen base module (train_qat_frozen_stem.py:86-89, 107-108, 166-178).

The fresh path refuses an existing run or execution directory, is planned for exactly ten updates and 220 presentations, retains the 100-update overall cap and 75 C/30-minute protection settings, and declares no automatic retry or continuation (train_qat_frozen_stem.py:92-112).

The wrapper copies only the previously passed cache receipt and verifies its exact hash; inherited prepare() then independently opens and validates that cache against the frozen dataset snapshot and pinned cache index (train_qat_frozen_stem.py:167-173; train_qat.py:42-55).

The new protocol changes only its name plus explicit frozen layer/fields and prior-update metadata. The starting FP32 checkpoint, maxabs package graph/scales/payload, dataset/content, replay schedule, cache identities, optimizer hyperparameters, microbatch 2 accumulation, and ten 22-sample orders remain inherited from the hash-pinned base runner.

The generic evaluator permits the wrapper's additional identity and protocol fields, requires the completed candidate identity in the export manifest, and consumes the corrected integration_check_v2 resume gate. Its fixed purpose string remains acceptable because experiment identity and frozen protocol are nested and compared exactly (evaluate_qat.py:41-122, 166-180).
